***Among Us*** is a 2018 [online multiplayer](Online_multiplayer "Online multiplayer") [social deduction game](Social_deduction_game "Social deduction game") developed and published by American game studio Innersloth. The game was inspired by the party game [Mafia](Mafia_(party_game) "Mafia (party game)") and the [science fiction](Science_fiction_film "Science fiction film") [horror](Horror_film "Horror film") film *[The Thing](The_Thing_(1982_film) "The Thing (1982 film)")*. The game allows for [cross-platform play](Cross-platform_play "Cross-platform play"); it was released on [iOS](IOS "IOS") and [Android](Android_(operating_system) "Android (operating system)") devices in June 2018 and on <Windows> later that year in November. A virtual reality adaptation, *[Among Us VR](Among_Us_VR "Among Us VR")*, was released on November 10, 2022.

*Among Us* takes place in [space-themed](Science_fiction "Science fiction") settings where players are colorful, armless cartoon astronauts. Each player takes on one of two roles: most are Crewmates, but a small number are [Impostors](Impostor "Impostor"). Crewmates work to complete assigned tasks in the game while identifying and voting out suspected Impostors (who appear identical to Crewmates) using social deduction, while Impostors have the objective of killing the Crewmates.

While the game was initially released in 2018 to little mainstream attention, it received a massive rise in popularity in 2020 due to many [Twitch](Twitch_(service) "Twitch (service)") [streamers](Online_streamer "Online streamer") and [YouTubers](YouTuber "YouTuber") playing it during the [COVID-19 pandemic](COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). **Xseed Games** is an American [video game](Video_game "Video game") company founded by former members of [Square Enix USA](Square_Enix_USA "Square Enix USA"). It later became a subsidiary of the Japanese game company [Marvelous](Marvelous_(company) "Marvelous (company)"), providing the localization and publishing services for video games and related materials.

## History

In 2007, AQ Interactive, Inc. announced the acquisition of Xseed Games, with share transfer before June.[[1]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-1) The deal was signed on April 24, and the share transfer was completed on June 26.[[2]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-2) Xseed Games joined the forces with [Marvelous Entertainment](Marvelous_Entertainment "Marvelous Entertainment") (MMV) to co-publish their games in [North America](North_America "North America") in 2008.[[3]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-3)[[4]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-4)[[5]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-5) At [E3 2008](E3_2008 "E3 2008"), MMV USA and Xseed Games distinguished the games that would be co-published under the agreement and the games that Xseed would publish separately.[[6]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-6)

In 2009 on April 1, AQ Interactive announced increasing its stake of Xseed Games from 55% to 90% on the day of announcement.[[7]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-7) On April 14, Xseed Games announced its partnership with [Japanese](Japan "Japan") developer [Nihon Falcom](Nihon_Falcom "Nihon Falcom") over localizing and publishing *[Ys Seven](Ys_Seven "Ys Seven")*, *[Ys: The Oath in Felghana](Ys%3A_The_Oath_in_Felghana "Ys: The Oath in Felghana")*, *[Ys I & II Chronicles](Ys_I_%26_II_Chronicles "Ys I & II Chronicles")*, and the *[Trails in the Sky](Trails_in_the_Sky "Trails in the Sky")* trilogy for the [PlayStation Portable](PlayStation_Portable "PlayStation Portable") in North America.[[8]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-8)[[9]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-9)

Xseed Games published *[Ys: The Oath in Felghana](Ys%3A_The_Oath_in_Felghana "Ys: The Oath in Felghana")* and *[Ys Origin](Ys_Origin "Ys Origin")* on the [Steam](Steam_(service) "Steam (service)") digital distribution platform in 2012 as their first release.[[10]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-10) In March 2013, [Index Corporation](Index_Corporation "Index Corporation")'s <Atlus> Online Division online business unit was purchased by Marvelous AQL and transferred to Xseed.[[11]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-11) Later on April 6, Xseed Games announced its business name was changed to Marvelous USA, Inc.[[12]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-12)

In 2019, former Xseed localization producer Brittany Avery discovered that she was not credited for her work on the enhanced PlayStation 4 port of *[The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel](The_Legend_of_Heroes%3A_Trails_of_Cold_Steel "The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel")* after leaving the company the previous year. As a result, Xseed revealed their policy of not crediting staff members in games if they are no longer employed at the company at the time it releases. **Xseed Games** is an American [video game](Video_game "Video game") company founded by former members of [Square Enix USA](Square_Enix_USA "Square Enix USA"). It later became a subsidiary of the Japanese game company [Marvelous](Marvelous_(company) "Marvelous (company)"), providing the localization and publishing services for video games and related materials.

## History

In 2007, AQ Interactive, Inc. announced the acquisition of Xseed Games, with share transfer before June.[[1]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-1) The deal was signed on April 24, and the share transfer was completed on June 26.[[2]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-2) Xseed Games joined the forces with [Marvelous Entertainment](Marvelous_Entertainment "Marvelous Entertainment") (MMV) to co-publish their games in [North America](North_America "North America") in 2008.[[3]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-3)[[4]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-4)[[5]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-5) At [E3 2008](E3_2008 "E3 2008"), MMV USA and Xseed Games distinguished the games that would be co-published under the agreement and the games that Xseed would publish separately.[[6]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-6)

In 2009 on April 1, AQ Interactive announced increasing its stake of Xseed Games from 55% to 90% on the day of announcement.[[7]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-7) On April 14, Xseed Games announced its partnership with [Japanese](Japan "Japan") developer [Nihon Falcom](Nihon_Falcom "Nihon Falcom") over localizing and publishing *[Ys Seven](Ys_Seven "Ys Seven")*, *[Ys: The Oath in Felghana](Ys%3A_The_Oath_in_Felghana "Ys: The Oath in Felghana")*, *[Ys I & II Chronicles](Ys_I_%26_II_Chronicles "Ys I & II Chronicles")*, and the *[Trails in the Sky](Trails_in_the_Sky "Trails in the Sky")* trilogy for the [PlayStation Portable](PlayStation_Portable "PlayStation Portable") in North America.[[8]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-8)[[9]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-9)

Xseed Games published *[Ys: The Oath in Felghana](Ys%3A_The_Oath_in_Felghana "Ys: The Oath in Felghana")* and *[Ys Origin](Ys_Origin "Ys Origin")* on the [Steam](Steam_(service) "Steam (service)") digital distribution platform in 2012 as their first release.[[10]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-10) In March 2013, [Index Corporation](Index_Corporation "Index Corporation")'s <Atlus> Online Division online business unit was purchased by Marvelous AQL and transferred to Xseed.[[11]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-11) Later on April 6, Xseed Games announced its business name was changed to Marvelous USA, Inc.[[12]](Xseed_Games#cite_note-12)

In 2019, former Xseed localization producer Brittany Avery discovered that she was not credited for her work on the enhanced PlayStation 4 port of *[The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel](The_Legend_of_Heroes%3A_Trails_of_Cold_Steel "The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel")* after leaving the company the previous year. As a result, Xseed revealed their policy of not crediting staff members in games if they are no longer employed at the company at the time it releases.
